claim: DUCT is a method for double resin casting micro computed tomography that enables visualization and digitalization of two tubular systems in 3D.
source: We aimed to develop a robust technology to visualize, digitalize, and segment the architecture of two tubular systems in 3D: double resin casting micro computed tomography (DUCT).
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the development of DUCT as a technology for 3D visualization of two tubular systems.

claim: Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice are a mouse model for Alagille syndrome characterized by intrahepatic bile duct paucity.
source: As proof of principle, we applied DUCT to a mouse model for Alagille syndrome (Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice), characterized by intrahepatic bile duct paucity, that can spontaneously generate a biliary system in adulthood.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice as a model for Alagille syndrome with bile duct paucity.

claim: Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice can spontaneously generate a biliary system in adulthood.
source: As proof of principle, we applied DUCT to a mouse model for Alagille syndrome (Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice), characterized by intrahepatic bile duct paucity, that can spontaneously generate a biliary system in adulthood.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice can spontaneously generate a biliary system in adulthood.

claim: DUCT identified increased central biliary branching in Jag1Ndr/Ndr liver as a compensatory process.
source: DUCT identified increased central biliary branching and peripheral bile duct tortuosity as two compensatory processes occurring in distinct regions of Jag1Ndr/Ndr liver, leading to full reconstitution of wild-type biliary volume and phenotypic recovery.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that DUCT identified increased central biliary branching as a compensatory process.

claim: DUCT identified peripheral bile duct tortuosity in Jag1Ndr/Ndr liver as a compensatory process.
source: DUCT identified increased central biliary branching and peripheral bile duct tortuosity as two compensatory processes occurring in distinct regions of Jag1Ndr/Ndr liver, leading to full reconstitution of wild-type biliary volume and phenotypic recovery.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that DUCT identified peripheral bile duct tortuosity as a compensatory process.

source: DUCT is thus a powerful new technology for 3D analysis, which can reveal novel phenotypes and provide a standardized method of defining liver architecture in mouse models.

claim: Alagille syndrome is a congenital disorder affecting multiple organs, including the hepatic and cardiovascular systems.
source: Alagille syndrome (ALGS) is a congenital disorder affecting multiple organs, including the hepatic and cardiovascular systems (Spinner et al., 1993; Mašek and Andersson, 2017).
evidence: The introduction cites references for the description of Alagille syndrome.

claim: Alagille syndrome is usually caused by mutations in the Notch ligand JAGGED1.
source: The disease is usually caused by mutations in the Notch ligand JAGGED1 (JAG1, OMIM: ALGS1 [Oda et al., 1997; Li et al., 1997; Gilbert et al., 2019]) or, less frequently, in the receptor NOTCH2 (OMIM: ALGS2 [Spinner et al., 1993; McDaniell et al., 2006]), and is chiefly characterized by intrahepatic peripheral bile duct paucity (Alagille et al., 1975; Riely et al., 1979).
evidence: The introduction cites references for the genetic causes of Alagille syndrome.

claim: Alagille syndrome is less frequently caused by mutations in the receptor NOTCH2.
source: The disease is usually caused by mutations in the Notch ligand JAGGED1 (JAG1, OMIM: ALGS1 [Oda et al., 1997; Li et al., 1997; Gilbert et al., 2019]) or, less frequently, in the receptor NOTCH2 (OMIM: ALGS2 [Spinner et al., 1993; McDaniell et al., 2006]), and is chiefly characterized by intrahepatic peripheral bile duct paucity (Alagille et al., 1975; Riely et al., 1979).
evidence: The introduction cites references for the genetic causes of Alagille syndrome.

claim: Bile duct development is regulated by portal vein mesenchyme.

claim: On average one abruptly ending BD per lobe was observed in Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers.

claim: Abruptly ending bile ducts in Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers were confirmed in serial liver sections.

claim: Abruptly terminating bile ducts were detected in liver sections from patients with mild Alagille syndrome.

evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 2C shows the data.

claim: 1.5% of Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts are placed 0.5–1.26 mm away from a portal vein.

claim: Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts sometimes traversed the parenchyma to join another portal vein branch.

evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 3B shows the data.

claim: Increased BD-PV distance and parenchymal bile ducts were validated in histological sections.
source: Both the increased BD-PV distance and parenchymal bile ducts were validated in histological sections, in which Jag1+/+ bile ducts were in close proximity to, or embedded in portal vein mesenchyme (Figure 3E left panel, asterisk).

claim: Jag1+/+ bile ducts were in close proximity to, or embedded in portal vein mesenchyme.
source: Both the increased BD-PV distance and parenchymal bile ducts were validated in histological sections, in which Jag1+/+ bile ducts were in close proximity to, or embedded in portal vein mesenchyme (Figure 3E left panel, asterisk).

claim: Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts were confirmed to be present outside of the portal vein mesenchyme area.
source: In contrast, Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts were confirmed to be present outside of the portal vein mesenchyme area (Figure 3E middle panel, double arrow) or even in the liver parenchyma close to the edge of the liver (Figure 3E right panel).

claim: Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts were confirmed to be present in the liver parenchyma close to the edge of the liver.
source: In contrast, Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts were confirmed to be present outside of the portal vein mesenchyme area (Figure 3E middle panel, double arrow) or even in the liver parenchyma close to the edge of the liver (Figure 3E right panel).

claim: Parenchymal bile ducts were detected in liver samples from patients with severe and mild Alagille syndrome.
source: Parenchymal bile ducts were also detected in liver samples from patients with severe and mild Alagille syndrome (Figure 3F) but not in control human liver.

claim: Parenchymal bile ducts were not detected in control human liver.
source: Parenchymal bile ducts were also detected in liver samples from patients with severe and mild Alagille syndrome (Figure 3F) but not in control human liver.

claim: Postnatal bile duct formation does not rely on close proximity to portal vein mesenchyme and may occur independent of signals from portal vein mesenchyme.
source: Our data showing biliary cells in the parenchyma and bile ducts far from portal veins in Jag1Ndr/Ndr liver and liver from patients with Alagille syndrome thus suggest that postnatal bile duct formation does not rely on close proximity to portal vein mesenchyme and may occur independent of signals from portal vein mesenchyme.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this conclusion.

claim: There were no differences in the absolute numbers of branch points in Jag1+/+ and Jag1Ndr/Ndr systems.
source: We did not identify any differences in the absolute numbers of branch points in Jag1+/+ and Jag1Ndr/Ndr systems, again suggesting that de novo biliary growth generally reconstituted a full-volume, well-branched biliary tree (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1 shows the data.

claim: De novo biliary growth generally reconstituted a full-volume, well-branched biliary tree.
source: We did not identify any differences in the absolute numbers of branch points in Jag1+/+ and Jag1Ndr/Ndr systems, again suggesting that de novo biliary growth generally reconstituted a full-volume, well-branched biliary tree (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this conclusion, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1 shows the data.

claim: Jag1+/+ bile ducts branched adjacent to portal vein branch points (defined as within 0.5 mm).
source: Indeed, Jag1+/+ bile ducts (Figure 4B left panel, blue arrowhead) branched adjacent to portal vein branch points (magenta arrowhead, defined as within 0.5 mm).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 4B shows the data.

claim: Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts branched further from portal vein branch points.
source: In contrast, Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts (Figure 4B middle panel, blue arrowhead) branched further from portal vein branch points (magenta arrowhead), or independent of portal vein branch points (blue arrow in Figure 4B, and data in 4C; independence defined as distance >0.54 mm).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 4B shows the data.

claim: Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts branched independent of portal vein branch points (independence defined as distance >0.54 mm).
source: In contrast, Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts (Figure 4B middle panel, blue arrowhead) branched further from portal vein branch points (magenta arrowhead), or independent of portal vein branch points (blue arrow in Figure 4B, and data in 4C; independence defined as distance >0.54 mm).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 4B and 4C show the data.

claim: On average, 1.3% of Jag1+/+ bile ducts branch points were further than 0.5 mm from the nearest portal vein branch point.
source: On average, 1.3% of Jag1+/+ bile ducts branch points and 8.6% of Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile duct branch points were further than 0.5 mm from the nearest portal vein branch point (Figure 4C).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantification, and Figure 4C shows the data.

claim: On average, 8.6% of Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile duct branch points were further than 0.5 mm from the nearest portal vein branch point.
source: On average, 1.3% of Jag1+/+ bile ducts branch points and 8.6% of Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile duct branch points were further than 0.5 mm from the nearest portal vein branch point (Figure 4C).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantification, and Figure 4C shows the data.

claim: Jag1+/+ bile ducts branched at the same point as portal veins branch in histological liver sections.
source: Jag1+/+ bile ducts (Figure 4D top panel, blue arrowhead) indeed branched at the same point as portal veins branch (magenta arrowhead).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 4D shows the data.

claim: In Jag1Ndr/Ndr liver bile ducts might bifurcate in the absence of portal vein branching.
source: In contrast, in Jag1Ndr/Ndr liver bile ducts might bifurcate in the absence of portal vein branching (Figure 4D bottom panel, blue arrow).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 4D shows the data.

claim: In normal human liver, biliary branching occurred close to portal vein bifurcation.
source: In normal human liver, biliary branching occurred close to portal vein bifurcation (Figure 4E top panel, blue arrowheads, PV branching within 25 μm in this example, branching not shown).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 4E shows the data.

claim: In patients with severe Alagille syndrome, biliary branching could be seen independent of portal vein branching.
source: In patients with severe Alagille syndrome, biliary branching could be seen independent of portal vein branching (Figure 4E middle panel, blue arrows), the nearest portal vein branch point for this bile duct was 13 sections hilar (circa 65 μm earlier).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 4E shows the data.

claim: Independent bile duct branching was detected in patients with mild Alagille syndrome.
source: We also detected independent bile duct branching in patients with mild Alagille syndrome (Figure 4E bottom panel, blue arrows).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 4E shows the data.

claim: DUCT revealed similar numbers of branch points in Jag1+/+ and Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers.
source: In conclusion, DUCT revealed dual system 3D architectural phenotypes: (1) similar numbers of branch points in Jag1+/+ and Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers but (2) a greater distance between portal vein and bile duct branch points in Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this conclusion.

claim: DUCT revealed a greater distance between portal vein and bile duct branch points in Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers.
source: In conclusion, DUCT revealed dual system 3D architectural phenotypes: (1) similar numbers of branch points in Jag1+/+ and Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers but (2) a greater distance between portal vein and bile duct branch points in Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this conclusion.

claim: Bile ducts in patients with Alagille syndrome displayed similar branching abnormalities, corroborating the architectural independence from portal vein patterning.
source: Bile ducts in patients with Alagille syndrome displayed similar branching abnormalities, corroborating the architectural independence from portal vein patterning.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this conclusion.

claim: The liver lobe data were separated into three equivalent regions using portal vein branch generation number and lengths as a proxy for hilum/intermediate/periphery.
source: In order to define anatomy correctly for differently sized livers, the liver lobe data were separated into three equivalent regions using portal vein branch generation number and lengths as a proxy for hilum/intermediate/periphery. These regions were denoted region 1 (R1 enriched for hilar region), 2 (R2, intermediate), and 3 (R3, peripheral-enriched) (Figure 5A).
evidence: The results section explicitly describes the method for region separation, and Figure 5A illustrates this.

claim: The average branch length of the portal vein was shorter in Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers, resulting in significantly smaller portal vein region sizes.
source: The average branch length of the portal vein was shorter in Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers, resulting in significantly smaller portal vein region sizes (Figure 5B middle panel), reflecting the overall smaller size of the mice and livers.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 5B shows the data.

claim: Biliary region size was similar in the 1st and 2nd region of wild type and Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice.
source: Using the regions defined by the portal venous system, biliary region size was similar in the 1 st and 2nd region of wild type and Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice, while region three was smaller in both animal groups due to resin not penetrating ducts < 5 μm (Figure 5B right panel, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 5B shows the data.

claim: Region three was smaller in both Jag1+/+ and Jag1Ndr/Ndr animal groups due to resin not penetrating ducts < 5 μm.
source: Using the regions defined by the portal venous system, biliary region size was similar in the 1 st and 2nd region of wild type and Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice, while region three was smaller in both animal groups due to resin not penetrating ducts < 5 μm (Figure 5B right panel, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 5B shows the data.

claim: Two out of three Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice had a marked reduction in biliary region size in R3.
source: Two out of three Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice had a marked reduction in biliary region size in R3, while one had an increase, reflecting the somewhat variable phenotype manifested by both the patients and the mouse model.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: One out of three Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice had an increase in biliary region size in R3.
source: Two out of three Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice had a marked reduction in biliary region size in R3, while one had an increase, reflecting the somewhat variable phenotype manifested by both the patients and the mouse model.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Portal vein segments shortened as expected with each generation in both Jag1+/+ and Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers.
source: We analyzed the portal vein and biliary branch lengths within each region and found that portal vein segments shortened as expected with each generation in both Jag1+/+ and Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers (Figure 5C middle panel).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 5C shows the data.

claim: Jag1+/+ bile ducts followed the stereotype branching principle where branch lengths shorten with each generation.
source: Jag1+/+ bile ducts followed the same stereotype branching principle, but Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts branch lengths were significantly shorter in regions 1 and 2, and uniform across the hierarchy of branches (Figure 5C right panel).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 5C shows the data.

claim: Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts branch lengths were significantly shorter in regions 1 and 2, and uniform across the hierarchy of branches.
source: Jag1+/+ bile ducts followed the same stereotype branching principle, but Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts branch lengths were significantly shorter in regions 1 and 2, and uniform across the hierarchy of branches (Figure 5C right panel).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 5C shows the data.

claim: On average, 9% of Jag1+/+ portal vein branches fell into R1, 66% into R2% and 25% into R3.
source: We further analyzed the distribution of number of branches in the three regions and discovered that, on average, 9% of Jag1+/+ portal vein branches fell into R1, 66% into R2% and 25% into R3, with a similar distribution in Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers (Figure 5D middle panel).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantification, and Figure 5D shows the data.

claim: Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers had a similar portal vein branch distribution to Jag1+/+ livers.
source: We further analyzed the distribution of number of branches in the three regions and discovered that, on average, 9% of Jag1+/+ portal vein branches fell into R1, 66% into R2% and 25% into R3, with a similar distribution in Jag1Ndr/Ndr livers (Figure 5D middle panel).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 5D shows the data.

claim: Jag1+/+ biliary branch distribution was, on average, 16% in R1, 66% in R2% and 18% in R3.
source: Mirroring the wild type portal venous branch distribution, Jag1+/+ biliary branch distribution was, on average, 16% in R1, 66% in R2% and 18% in R3.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantification.

claim: Jag1Ndr/Ndr biliary branch distribution was shifted, with 44% in R1, 44% in R2% and 12% in R3.
source: Jag1Ndr/Ndr biliary branch distribution was shifted, with 44% in R1, 44% in R2% and 12% in R3 (Figure 5D right panel).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantification, and Figure 5D shows the data.

claim: The distribution of biliary branches number was highly heterogeneous among the different Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice.
source: The distribution of biliary branches number was highly heterogeneous among the different Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: Low-generation number biliary segments were shorter and more numerous than expected, suggesting that ectopic regenerative branching and/or incorporation of de novo generated biliary cells, occurs in region 1.
source: DUCT pipeline is compatible with multiple image analysis software programs. Here, we used ImageJ to address the branching length over branching generations, and our data collectively indicated that low-generation number biliary segments were shorter and more numerous than expected, suggesting that ectopic regenerative branching and/or incorporation of de novo generated biliary cells, occurs in region 1.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this conclusion.

claim: Peripheral branching, which may be undetectable if biliary diameters are under 5 μm, cannot be excluded.
source: However, peripheral branching, which may be undetectable if biliary diameters are under 5 μm, cannot be excluded.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this caveat.

claim: 3D reconstruction of portal vein vasculature and the biliary network revealed straight Jag1+/+ bile ducts.
source: 3D reconstruction of portal vein vasculature and the biliary network revealed straight Jag1+/+ bile ducts (Figure 6A top panel), whereas Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts were tortuous (Figure 6A bottom panel), especially in the liver periphery.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 6A shows the data.

claim: 3D reconstruction of portal vein vasculature and the biliary network revealed tortuous Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts, especially in the liver periphery.

claim: Several tortuous bile ducts were found in patients with mild Alagille syndrome.

evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding, and Figure 6C shows the data.

claim: No tortuous bile ducts were detected in patients with severe Alagille syndrome.
source: We further assessed biliary tortuosity in patients with mild Alagille syndrome and found several tortuous bile ducts (Figure 6C); however, we did not detect any tortuous bile ducts in patients with severe Alagille syndrome (data not shown).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: The curved and chord lengths of the entire system, and the main branch alone did not differ for portal venous or biliary systems in Jag1+/+ and Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice.
source: The curved and chord lengths of the entire system, and the main branch alone did not differ for portal venous or biliary systems in Jag1+/+ and Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–G).

claim: The BD:PV ratio was not significantly different for curved or chord length.

claim: Biliary tortuosity was increased by 50% in Jag1Ndr/Ndr mice.

claim: Biliary tortuosity was greatest in the Jag1Ndr/Ndr liver periphery, with a 140% increase in R3.

claim: Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts recovered wild-type lengths postnatally, with a pronounced increase in peripheral tortuosity.
source: In summary, DUCT allowed analysis of curved and chord length measurements for the entire or defined regions of the injected trees. Jag1Ndr/Ndr bile ducts recovered wild-type lengths postnatally, with a pronounced increase in peripheral tortuosity.

source: Precisely defining the three-dimensional (3D) architecture of healthy and diseased organs is a fundamental aspect of biology, and improved imaging methods would allow stricter characterization of animal models for human diseases.
